records.text: He did not gain control of the government; receiving shame as the outcome of his plot, he again went away as a fugitive into the Ammonite country.

In the end he met a disastrous conclusion. Accused before Aretas, ruler of the Arabs, he fled from city to city, pursued by everyone, hated as a deserter of the laws and abhorred as the executioner of his homeland and fellow citizens, until he was driven into Egypt.
He who had made many strangers to their homeland perished in a foreign land, having sailed to the Lacedaemonians in the hope of obtaining shelter because of their kinship.
When news of these events reached the king, he concluded that Judea was in revolt. He therefore broke camp in Egypt, savage in spirit, took the city by force of arms,
and ordered the soldiers to cut down without mercy those they met and slaughter those who went up into the houses.
In the space of three days eighty thousand were lost: forty thousand in the acts of violence, and no fewer than those slaughtered were sold.
Not content with this, he dared to enter the holiest temple in all the earth, with Menelaus as guide—the man who had become a traitor to both the laws and his homeland.
With defiled hands he took the sacred vessels, and with profane hands swept away the gifts other kings had dedicated for the enhancement, glory and honour of the place.
O you who build your house without righteousness and your upper rooms without judgment! He works through his neighbor without payment and will not give him his wages.
You built yourself a well-proportioned house, airy upper rooms set apart by windows, paneled with cedar and painted with red ocher.
Will you reign because you are provoked in Ahaz your father? They will not eat or drink. It was better for you to do judgment and good righteousness.
They did not know; they did not judge a case for the lowly or a case for the poor. Is this not your failing to know Me? says the Lord.
Behold, neither your eyes nor your heart are good; instead they are directed toward your greed, innocent blood to shed it, wrongdoing, and murder to commit it.
He cried into my ears with a loud voice, saying, “The city’s retribution has drawn near.” Each had the implements of destruction in his hand.

And behold, six men came from the direction of the high gate facing north, each with an axe in his hand. One man among them wore a full-length robe, with a sapphire belt at his waist. They entered and stood beside the bronze altar.
The glory of the God of Israel, which had been upon the cherubim, rose from them to the forecourt of the house. He called the man wearing the full-length robe, who had the belt at his waist,
and said to him, “Pass through the midst of Jerusalem and put the sign upon the foreheads of the men who sigh deeply and grieve over all the lawlessness being committed within her.”
He said to them, “Defile the house and fill the roads with the dead as you go out, and strike.”
As they struck, I fall upon my face and cried aloud and said, “Alas, Lord! Art Thou obliterating the survivors of Israel as Thou pourest out Thy wrath upon Jerusalem?”

He said to me, “The injustice of the house of Israel and Judah has grown very, very great, because the land is full of many peoples, and the city full of injustice and uncleanness. For they said, ‘The Lord has abandoned the land; the Lord does not look upon it.’
My eye will not spare, nor will I have mercy. I have brought their ways upon their heads.”
And behold, the man wearing the full-length robe, with the belt fastened at his waist, answered, saying, “I have done as Thou didst command me.”
A certain Eleazar, one of the foremost scribes, a man already advanced in age and most handsome in appearance, was being forced to open his mouth and eat pork.
Choosing a glorious death rather than a defiled life, he went of his own accord to the torture frame,
having spat it out, as those ought to approach who persevere in refusing things it is unlawful to taste, even for love of life.

Those appointed to oversee the unlawful eating of sacrificial entrails, because of their long acquaintance with the man, took him aside and urged him to bring meat prepared by himself that he could lawfully use, but to pretend that he was eating the sacrificial meat ordered by the king.
By doing this, they said, he would be released from death and receive humane treatment because of his old friendship with them.
“For it is unworthy of our age to pretend, lest many of the young suppose that Eleazar, at ninety years of age, has gone over to foreign ways,
and through my pretence, for the sake of a brief and momentary life, they themselves be led astray because of me, and I acquire defilement and a stain upon my old age.
For even if I now escape the punishment inflicted by human beings, neither living nor dead shall I escape the hands of the Almighty.
Therefore, by departing this life courageously now, I shall show myself worthy of my old age,
and leave the young a noble example of dying willingly and nobly for the revered and holy laws.” After saying this, he went immediately to the torture frame.
Those who led him changed their goodwill of a little earlier into hostility, because they considered his preceding words madness.

As he was about to die under the blows, he groaned and said, “It is clear to the Lord, who possesses holy knowledge, that although I could have been released from death, I endure harsh bodily pains under the scourging. Yet in my soul I gladly suffer these things because I fear Him.”
Thus he departed in this way, leaving his own death as an example of nobility and a memorial of virtue, not only to the young but also to the greater part of the nation.
A patient man is better than a strong man, and one who controls anger is better than one who captures a city.
Everything comes into the laps of the unjust, but all righteous things are from the Lord.
You have not gathered in youth; how could you find anything in your old age?
It also happened that seven brothers were arrested with their mother and compelled by the king to partake of forbidden pork, while being tortured with whips and sinew lashes.
One of them became their spokesman and said, “What do you intend to ask and learn of us? We are ready to die rather than transgress our ancestral laws.”
The king became furious and ordered pans and cauldrons to be heated.
When they were immediately heated, he ordered the tongue of their spokesman cut out, and that he be scalped and his extremities cut off while the other brothers and their mother watched.

When he had been rendered completely helpless, the king ordered him brought to the fire, still breathing, and fried in a pan. As the vapor from the pan spread far, they encouraged one another with their mother to die nobly, saying,
“The Lord God watches, and in truth He has compassion on us, as Moses explained in the song that bears witness against us to our face, saying, ‘And He will have compassion on His servants.’”

After the first had departed in this manner, they brought the second for their mockery. Tearing the skin from his head together with his hair, they asked, “Will you eat before your body is punished limb by limb?”
He answered in his ancestral language, “No.” Therefore he too received the ensuing torture, as the first had.
And when he was at his last breath, he said, “You, accursed one, release us from this present life; but the King of the world shall raise us, who die for His laws, unto everlasting renewal of life.”
After him the third was mocked. When asked for his tongue, he quickly put it out and fearlessly stretched forth his hands.
He nobly said, “I received these from heaven, and for His laws I disregard them; from Him I hope to receive them again.”
When he too had departed, they tortured the fourth in the same manner, tormenting him.
As he was about to die, he said, “It is preferable, when dying at human hands, to look for the hopes given by God, to be raised again by Him. But for you there shall be no resurrection to life.”
The next day their rulers, elders, and scribes gathered in Jerusalem,
together with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and all who belonged to the high-priestly family.
They made them stand in their midst and asked, “By what power or by what name did you do this?”
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, “Rulers of the people and elders,
if we are being examined today concerning a good deed done to a disabled man, and by what means he has been made well,

let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead—in Him this man stands before you in good health.
He is the stone despised by you, the builders, which has become the cornerstone.
Salvation is in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among human beings by which we must be saved.”
For the man in whom this sign of healing had occurred was more than forty years old.
